reference_drawer.title: 📖 Midpoint & Ratios Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Essential formulas for midpoints, trisections, parallelogram vertices, quarter division, and ratio finding.

items.rule: The midpoint averages corresponding x- and y-coordinates.
items.example: Use denominator 2 because the segment is split into two equal parts.

items.rule: Internal trisection points use ratios 1:2 and 2:1.
items.example: The denominator is 3 because the ratio parts sum to 3.

items.rule: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
items.example: Set the x- and y-coordinates of the two diagonal midpoints equal.

items.rule: Two successive midpoint operations on AM and MB create the quarter points.
items.example: The three internal points occur in the order Q₁,M,Q₃.

items.rule: Use k:1 when the internal division ratio is unknown.
items.example: Substitute a known coordinate and solve for k.

items.rule: A point on the x-axis has y=0; a point on the y-axis has x=0.
items.example: Solve k from the zero-coordinate equation, then calculate the other coordinate.

concepts.title: 1. Midpoint Formula
concepts.subtitle: Average corresponding endpoint coordinates
concepts.summary: The midpoint of a segment is found by averaging the x-coordinates and averaging the y-coordinates of the endpoints.

concepts.title: 2. Trisection Points
concepts.subtitle: Internal ratios 1:2 and 2:1
concepts.summary: The two trisection points are obtained by applying the internal section formula with ratios 1:2 and 2:1.

points.text: Use AP:PB = 1:2 for the first point.
Use AQ:QB = 2:1 for the second point.

concepts.title: 3. Fourth Vertex of a Parallelogram
concepts.subtitle: Diagonals bisect each other
concepts.summary: The fourth vertex is recovered by equating the midpoint coordinates of diagonals AC and BD.

points.text: Set it equal to the midpoint of BD and solve.

concepts.trap: Using a side midpoint or assuming equal adjacent sides.

concepts.title: 4. Dividing a Segment into Four Equal Parts
concepts.subtitle: Successive midpoint construction
concepts.summary: First find the midpoint of AB. Then bisect AM and MB to obtain the first and third quarter points.

points.text: Find M, the midpoint of AB.

concepts.trap: Using the trisection formula instead of successive midpoints.

concepts.title: 5. Finding the Ratio k:1
concepts.subtitle: Recover an unknown internal division ratio
concepts.summary: Assume AP:PB=k:1, substitute the known point into the section formula, and solve for k.

points.text: Use one known coordinate to isolate k.

concepts.title: 6. Axis Division of a Segment
concepts.subtitle: Find the ratio and the intercept point
concepts.summary: For an x-axis division point set y=0. For a y-axis division point set x=0, solve k, then calculate the remaining coordinate.

points.text: Solve the section-formula numerator for k.
Substitute k to get the division coordinates.
